extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners (prosecution personnel)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures in the MPEP governing extensions of time, petitions to reset reply periods, handling of late replies, and formal/express abandonment of patent applications. Covers who may file/authorize petitions, required evidence, fee handling, and effects on prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive filing when petition omitted but prior authorizations exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who inadvertently omitted a petition but have (A) previously filed a written request to treat a reply requiring an extension of time as incorporating a petition for such extension of time; (B) previously filed an authorization to charge all required fees, fees under 37 CFR 1.17, or all required extension of time fees; or (C) submitted the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(a) with the reply, may be treated as having filed the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office strongly recommends including a written petition in reply to avoid processing delays. A sample short petition is given. See also 37 CFR 1.136(a)(2) — date on which petition and fee filed is the date for determining the extension period. Use a written petition where possible to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date for determining extension period (37 CFR 1.136(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which the petition and the fee have been filed is the date for purposes of determining the period of extension and the corresponding amount of the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.136(a) need not be accompanied by a reply (e.g., when needed for copendency). However, a reply must be filed prior to expiration of the period of extension to avoid abandonment (see 35 U.S.C. 133 and 37 CFR 1.135).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office practice to construe petition as requesting appropriate period when fee authorization present
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition requests an insufficient extension period such that the petition would be filed outside the so-extended period for reply, but the period could be further extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a) such that the petition would be filed within the further extended period, the Office will construe the petition as requesting the appropriate extension if the petition or application contains an authorization to charge extension fees or fees under 37 CFR 1.17 to a deposit account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a 2-month petition filed 4.5 months after an appeal may be treated as requesting a 3-month extension if fee authorization is present. This also applies to constructive petitions under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition filed in continuing application must specifically refer and include conditional abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition for an extension of time (or petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137) in which a continuing application is filed in lieu of a reply should specifically refer to the filing of the continuing application and include an express abandonment of the prior application conditioned upon granting of the petition and granting of a filing date to the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An extension will not be effected in the prior application by filing a petition, fee, or fee authorization in the continuing application — the petition must be directed toward and filed in the application to which it pertains in accordance with 37 CFR 1.4 and 1.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late reply without petition/fee is not timely until petition and fee submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reply is filed after the set period for reply has expired and no petition or fee accompanies it, the reply will not be accepted as timely until the petition (which may be a constructive petition under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3)) and the appropriate fee are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Office action with 3-month period; applicant replies in 4th month including only a 1-month petition — reply not acceptable until fee filed. If fee filed in 5th month, additional fee for 2nd month extension required to render reply timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extension needed for supplemental reply if complete first reply was timely
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension under 37 CFR 1.136 is not necessary when submitting a supplemental reply to an Office action if a complete first reply was timely filed in reply to the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental matters that merely supplement a timely first reply do not require an extension under 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for cause under 37 CFR 1.136(b) — timing and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When 37 CFR 1.136(a) is not applicable, extensions of time for cause under 37 CFR 1.136(b) may be possible; any such extension must be filed on or before the day on which the reply is due, and will be decided by the Technology Center (TC) Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extension under 1.136(b) can operate to extend time beyond the 6-month statutory period. Extensions under 1.136(a) or (b) are not available to extend the time periods set in a Notice of Allowability or later Office actions to submit an oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.63), formal drawings, or deposit of biological material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate petitions under 1.136(b) and returned duplicate procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for extension under 37 CFR 1.136(b) is filed in duplicate and accompanied by a stamped return-addressed envelope, the Office will indicate the action taken on the duplicate and return it promptly in the envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IFW processing, see IFW Manual. Utilization of this procedure is optional for applicant. The notation on the original (file record) should be signed by the person granting/denying the extension and the returned copy should show the name and title of that person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office notification and notation when request granted/denied or granted in part
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request is granted, no further action by the Office is necessary. When granted in part, the extent will be indicated on original and returned copy. When denied, the reason will be indicated on original and copy or a formal decision letter will be forwarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If granted, due date is computed from the date stamped/printed on the action (not original due date). Example provided showing date computation when periods extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-carried extension requests limited to Customer Service Window
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand-carried requests for extensions of time will no longer be accepted in the Technology Centers (TCs); hand-carried requests may only be delivered to the Customer Window at the Randolph Building address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Enclose a photocopy of current fee schedule with action so applicant can determine required fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for late replies suggesting extension (7.98 / 7.98.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.98 (Reply Is Late, Extension of Time Suggested) and 7.98.01 (Reply Is Late, Extension of Time Suggested, Pro Se) may be used where a reply is filed late but an extension of time is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 7.98.01 includes language advising pro se applicants of petition requirement under 37 CFR 1.136(a), fee per 1.17(a), that the date of reply/petition/fee is the date of reply and determines extension amount, and that no extension can carry reply beyond statutory SIX MONTHS; extensions under 1.136(a) cannot be for more than FIVE MONTHS beyond the time in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of reply period for first reply to a final rejection when advisory action timing varies
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant initially replies within 2 months to a final rejection setting a 3-month shortened period and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the end of the 3-month period, the period for reply for fee calculation purposes will be the date the advisory action is mailed, but in no event beyond 6 months from the date of the final rejection. Examiner must include specific mandatory language in each final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advisory action mailed before 3 months, shortened statutory period ends at 3 months. If mailed after 3 months, shortened period expires on mailing date of advisory action. Mandatory language requiring this explanation must be included in each final rejection. See MPEP § 706.07(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions to submit affidavits after final rejection are discretionary and do not guarantee admission
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant requests an extension to submit an affidavit after final rejection, granting the extension is without prejudice to the examiner's right to question why the affidavit was not earlier presented; if the showing is insufficient, the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit despite the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of extension merely keeps the application from becoming abandoned while applicant may present affidavit; prosecution to save must include timely, complete and proper action per 37 CFR 1.113. Admission or refusal to admit any amendment after final rejection will not operate to save application from abandonment. See also 37 CFR 1.116(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions of time after payment of issue fee (nonextendable period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory nonextendable time period for payment of the issue fee is 3 months from the date of the Notice of Allowance (35 U.S.C. 151).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informalities outstanding at allowance must be corrected and appropriate fees paid within the 3-month period. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 are not available to correct such informalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which period controls when two reply periods are running
rubrics_metrics.description: When two different periods for reply are running (one limited by the regular statutory period, the other by a limited period set in a subsequent Office action), the running of the first period is not suspended or affected by the ex parte limited time action or an appeal therefrom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cases copying patent claims see MPEP Chapter 2300 and Ex parte Milton. The date of the last unanswered Office action on claims other than copied patent claims is the controlling date of the statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules when due date falls on Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday (37 CFR 1.7 / 35 U.S.C. 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the day, or last day, for taking any action or paying any fee falls on Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the action may be taken or the fee paid on the next succeeding business day which is not a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calendar days are intended when periods specified. The provisional application's 12-month pendency is similarly extended. List of federal holidays provided; rules for when holiday falls on weekend and effect on USPTO closure; endorsements on file wrapper show the succeeding day and indicate the holiday.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reply period is restarted or reset due to Office error (incorrect citation/other error)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action contains an error that affects applicant's ability to reply and the error is called to the Office's attention within 1 month of the mail date, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply from the date the error is corrected, if applicant requests it. If called to attention within the reply period but more than 1 month after mailing, the Office may set a new period substantially equal to the time remaining (minimum 1 month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the error is called to attention after expiration of the period for reply, the period will not be restarted and extension fees will be required to render a reply timely. Remailing requires redating; a supplementary action establishes a new date from which statutory period runs. See MPEP § 707.05(g) and IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to reset period due to late receipt of Office action — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the period for reply to run from the date of receipt at the correspondence address when: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of receipt at correspondence address; (B) a substantial portion of the set reply period had elapsed on the date of receipt (e.g., at least 1 month of a 2- or 3-month period); and (C) petition includes evidence showing date of receipt at correspondence address and a statement explaining how the evidence establishes that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority to decide such petitions is delegated to the TC Director where the Office action was mailed by a Technology Center. See Notice “Petition to reset a period for response due to late receipt of a PTO action,” 1160 O.G. 14 (March 1, 1994). Extraordinary circumstances required if more than 2 months remaining in shortened statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to reset period due to postmark later than mail date — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the period for reply to run from the postmark date on the Office mailing envelope when: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of receipt at correspondence address; (B) reply period was for payment of the issue fee, or the reply period set was 1 month or 30 days; and (C) petition includes evidence of date of receipt, copy of the envelope showing postmark date, and a statement describing receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.8 and 1.10 apply to filing these petitions. The Office will evaluate facts to ensure delay was in mail rather than delayed after receipt in the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment by failure to reply within time (37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to reply within the time period provided under §§ 1.134 and 1.136, the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise. Prosecution to save an application from abandonment must include a complete and proper reply as the condition of the application may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission or refusal to admit an amendment after final rejection or any amendment not responsive to the last action will not operate to save the application from abandonment. Under 1.135(c), a bona fide attempt that inadvertently omitted some compliance may be given a new time period to supply the omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment requirements and procedures (37 CFR 1.138)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be expressly abandoned by filing a written declaration identifying the application; such a written declaration must be signed by a party authorized under § 1.33(b) (or other specified exceptions). Express abandonment may not be recognized before date of issue or publication unless received in time to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.138(c) to avoid publication must include fee per 1.17(h) and be received more than four weeks prior to projected publication to have a chance of stopping publication; facsimile transmission to Pre-Grant Publication Division is suggested when projected publication is less than 3 months away. If issue fee has been paid, direct petition to Office of Petitions with petition to withdraw from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c). A properly signed letter becomes effective when an appropriate official acts on it; the Office should acknowledge receipt and compliance. A letter of express abandonment not timely filed (outside reply period) is placed in file but not formally entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution about amendments canceling all claims — not express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all claims, even if signed by applicant and assignee, is not an express abandonment and is regarded as nonresponsive and not a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will not enter such amendment without presenting new or substitute claims. The practice of 37 CFR 1.135(c) does not apply to such amendments; applicant should be notified as explained in MPEP §§ 714.03–714.05. Withdrawal of appeal by an attorney/agent not of record may be allowed except where withdrawal would result in abandonment (in which case withdrawal is an express abandonment).
